name: Apollo 11 — Lunar Landing
description: Apollo 11, 16-24 July 1969: launch through splashdown, with the Moon on its real geocentric ephemeris. Through the surface stay: launch, ascent, parking orbit, TLI, the trans-lunar coast, lunar orbit insertion, the LM undocking and powered descent to touchdown, and the EVA on the surface.

tracks.SOURCE: JPL Horizons target 301 (Moon), geocentric ICRF state vectors, DE441, 15-minute steps, 1969-07-16T13:32Z + 8 days

GET 000:00:00 to 100:39:53. Launch, ascent and TLI are a gravity-turn reconstruction trimmed onto the published TLI cutoff state (Apollo by the Numbers); the coast is Earth + Moon RK4 from that state, with MCC-2 solved onto the 111 km perilune. LOI-1 and LOI-2 are published SPS burns (887.8 and 56.0 m/s) with the delta-v solved onto the published 111 x 314 km and ~99 x 121 km orbits. The Moon ephemeris is JPL Horizons 301 (DE441). Phase 7 (130:09:00 -> splashdown): the trans-Earth coast is integrated (Earth + Moon) from the jettison state, with a solved TEI at 135:22:42 that arrives 121.92 km up (400 000 ft) descending at -6.5 deg at 195:03:05. The solved burn is 1562 m/s against the flown ~998 m/s: the reconstruction's lunar phase is not Apollo's, and the burn has to absorb that difference to hit the same corridor at the same second. The entry is a shaped reconstruction, not a lifting-entry guidance simulation: the vertical speed falls from 1 245 m/s at the interface to a 9 m/s chute descent and the horizontal speed from 10.9 km/s to walking pace, with the altitude and downrange integrated from those profiles (2627 km of downrange, peak deceleration 5.2 g, against the published 5.8 g). Position and velocity come from the same integrals, so they always agree. The Earth here is a fixed sphere at the frame origin: no rotation and no atmosphere model beyond the speed profile.

maneuvers.note: S-IVB restart, 5 m 57 s; dv is the achieved speed change (thrust integral 3.18 km/s)
Midcourse correction (real MCC-2 was 1.04 m/s). This value retargets the reconstructed TLI state onto the real 111 km perilune at LOI-1; RTN components are the solved burn in the frame at ignition.

SPS lunar orbit insertion, 291 s, ignited 158 s before perilune (a finite burn centred on perilune is what produces the published 111 x 314 km). Published dv 887.8 m/s; this value is solved onto the published apsides because the reconstructed arrival speed differs slightly from the real one.

Second SPS burn, 18 s. Published 56.0 m/s onto a ~99.5 x 121.5 km orbit; the solved RTN components are what this reconstruction needs from its slightly different orbital phase, and the result matches the published apsides.

Trans-Earth injection: solved (two components in the plane of the coast) so the free return reaches the entry interface at 121.92 km with a -6.5 deg flight path angle at 195:03:05. Published TEI is ~1 000 m/s.

tracks.SOURCE: LM ascent (124:22:01) through docking (128:03:00) and jettison (130:09:00). The ascent is integrated (RK4, Earth + Moon gravity) with the engine on a fixed pitch programme and the burn length solved for an 18 x 87 km orbit. The rendezvous is two impulses solved with a 6x6 Newton so Eagle reaches Columbia's reconstructed position and velocity at the docking time; the TPI epoch was scanned for the cheapest transfer and the total is ~115 m/s against the real ~55 m/s, because Apollo flew four small burns where this flies two large ones. After docking Eagle rides Columbia (one stack) until jettison, when a 0.6 m/s retrograde push separates them. The Moon translates only, so a lunar-fixed attitude is undefined; the ascent plane is the one containing the landing site and Columbia's velocity at liftoff.

maneuvers.note: Separation nudge away from COLUMBIA; the real undocking was a spring push, not a burn.
Separation burn to open the range after the inspection flyaround.
Descent orbit insertion, retrograde: 111 km orbit lowered to 15 x 111 km. Published 23.2 m/s; the solved value absorbs this reconstruction's orbit phase.
Powered descent, 755 s. dv is the integrated thrust of the shaped profile (peak 3.16 m/s2), not a flown guidance solution.

Ascent engine on a pitch programme: vertical at liftoff, tipping downrange over the first 60% of the burn (pitch curve exponent 0.45) dv is the speed gained; the engine's thrust acceleration is 3.20 m/s2 and the mean net acceleration here is 1.90 km/s, the difference being gravity loss. Burn length solved for an 18 x 87 km orbit (published insertion 18 x 87 km at ~1.86 km/s).

Terminal phase initiation, solved against COLUMBIA: the burn that starts the transfer. Published 24.6 m/s belongs to Apollo's four-burn rendezvous; one long transfer costs more, so this reconstruction spends 67 m/s here and 65 m/s braking.
Braking gate: matches COLUMBIA's velocity three minutes before docking so the final approach closes slowly.
Ascent stage jettisoned with a 0.6 m/s push so Eagle falls behind (it was deliberately deorbited later). No crew, no samples.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.description: Liftoff from Pad 39A, Kennedy Space Center, 13:32:00 UTC.

events.label: S-IC CUTOFF
events.description: First stage separates at about 67 km and 2.7 km/s.

events.label: S-II CUTOFF
events.description: Second stage separates at about 185 km.

events.label: EARTH ORBIT
events.description: S-IVB cutoff; 185 km parking orbit at 32.5 deg inclination.

events.label: TLI IGNITION
events.description: S-IVB restarts for translunar injection.

events.label: TLI / COAST
events.description: Translunar injection cutoff; 3.1-day coast to the Moon.

events.label: DOCKING
events.description: CSM Columbia turns, docks with the LM and extracts it from the S-IVB.

events.label: MCC-2
events.description: Midcourse correction, trims the coast onto the 111 km perilune.

events.label: LUNAR SOI
events.description: Entering the Moon's sphere of influence.

events.label: LOI-1
events.description: SPS retrograde burn (291 s) into a 111 x 314 km lunar orbit; ignition is just before perilune.

events.label: LUNAR ORBIT
events.description: LOI-1: lunar orbit insertion into a 111 x 314 km ellipse.

events.label: LOI-2
events.description: Second SPS burn, circularising to ~99 x 121 km.

events.label: UNDOCKING
events.description: EAGLE separates from COLUMBIA.

events.label: LM DESCENT
events.description: Eagle separates from Columbia and begins the descent to the surface.

events.label: DOI
events.description: Descent orbit insertion to 15 x 111 km.

events.label: PDI
events.description: Powered descent initiation at 15.2 km.

events.label: SURFACE
events.description: Touchdown in the Sea of Tranquility.

events.label: EVA START
events.description: Depressurisation complete, LM hatch opened.

events.label: FIRST STEP
events.description: Armstrong steps onto the lunar surface.

events.label: ASCENT
events.description: Eagle lifts off from the lunar surface.

events.label: DOCKED
events.description: Eagle docks with Columbia; the crew and the sample boxes transfer.

events.label: JETTISON
events.description: Ascent stage released. Columbia is alone for the trip home.

events.label: RETURN / ENTRY
events.description: Trans-Earth injection; 3-day coast home.

events.label: ENTRY INTERFACE
events.description: 400 000 ft, 11 km/s; the deorbit burn is behind and the atmosphere is ahead.

events.label: SPLASHDOWN
events.description: Pacific Ocean, 2660 km east of Wake Island.
